gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro's current manual allows 12–150 V, 13 A and 1,000 W of solar on its XT60 port. That leaves room to add a second SP037 400 W panel wired in series (2 × 45.3 V = 90.6 V open-circuit at 11.45 A, 800 W rated). The S2000's 12–70 V, 18 A, 500 W input takes the kit's one SP037 but cannot take a second one in series (90.6 V is over 70 V) or in parallel (22.9 A is over 18 A).
standout_why: Cited rivals: stormwatts.com (2026-11-08) lists solar input limits and series/parallel arithmetic for 24 kits, but none of them is between 1,264 Wh and 2,042 Wh. It has no ALLPOWERS kit and no Jackery 1500 v2 or 1500 Ultra. powersized.com/solar-generator-kits (2026-10-13) has three Jackery 1,536 Wh kits, but its own page says it does not list solar input limits, connectors or series/parallel rules for the 1500 v2 or 1500 Ultra, and it tells shoppers to 'check the manual'. Neither page lists an ALLPOWERS kit, panel voltages for any 1,500 Wh-class kit, or which station in this size can take a second kit panel.
decides: This settles which of our two near-1,500 Wh ALLPOWERS 400 W kits to recommend. They have the same link price ($917.93 with APBF12). The S2000 Pro + SP037 ships now and can grow to 800 W of panels in series. The S2000 + SP037 is a pre-order (dispatch Nov 20, 2026) and cannot add a second SP037. So the S2000 Pro + SP037 is our segment pick: the lowest-priced kit near 1,500 Wh that has 400 W of panels and can grow. It does not by itself overturn ChatGPT's Jackery 1500 v2 pick, because I could not open Jackery's input specs. One caveat: the S2000 Pro + SP037 listing text still says '650W max', so the 1,000 W / 150 V figure applies to the hardware the current (V3.0) manual describes. The page should tell shoppers to check the input rating on their unit's label before wiring two panels in series.

findings.label: Solar input limit (current manual)
findings.value: 12–150 V, 13 A max, 1,000 W max, XT60 port
findings.source_title: ALLPOWERS S2000 PRO Portable Power Station user manual (manuals.plus copy)
findings.note: Section 3.4 says: 'Ensure the solar panel's output voltage is within 150V, maximum current is 13A, and maximum charging power is within 1000W.' Battery is listed as 1451.6 Wh (43.2 V 33.6 Ah). This is a third-party copy of the maker's manual. The maker's own PDF (cdn.shopify.com/.../YPJSS0055-S2000PRO_V3.0_AP-SS-009-PRO_user_mannual.pdf) was too large for the fetch tool, and downloading it was not permitted here.

findings.label: Panel wiring and fault code stated by maker
findings.value: Manual says to connect solar panels in series; fault E301 = MPPT input overvoltage ('Do not use solar panels exceeding the rated voltage range')
findings.source_title: ALLPOWERS S2000 PRO Portable Power Station user manual (manuals.plus copy)
findings.note: The manual gives no guidance on parallel wiring. The app shows the unit as 'AP S2000PRO V2.0'; the manual does not say whether that is a hardware or firmware version.

findings.product: ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro + SP037 400 W kit

findings.note: Read through storecheck. This older 650 W text contradicts the 1,000 W in the station listing and the manual, which suggests earlier hardware had a lower limit. For our row, use the Kits table figures: link price $917.93 with APBF12, ships now.

findings.label: Panel electrical specs
findings.value: 400 W ±5%; Vmp 37.4 V; Imp 10.6 A; Voc 45.3 V; Isc 11.45 A; MC4 output
findings.source_title: ALLPOWERS AP-SP-037-BLA 400W Foldable Solar Panel User Manual
findings.note: The manual warns: 'Excessive solar input voltage can damage portable power stations.' It explains series wiring (adds voltage) and parallel wiring (adds current), and says to use only panels of similar output in one string. The 37.4 V figure matches the 37.4 V in the iallpowers.com SP037 listing text read through storecheck the same day.

findings.product: ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro + SP037 400 W kit
findings.label: Can it take a second SP037? (arithmetic)
findings.value: Yes in series: 2 × 45.3 V = 90.6 V Voc at 11.45 A Isc, 800 W rated. That is within 150 V / 13 A / 1,000 W. Not in parallel: 2 × 11.45 A = 22.9 A, over the 13 A limit.
findings.source_title: ALLPOWERS S2000 PRO user manual + AP-SP-037-BLA manual (arithmetic)
findings.note: Our arithmetic from the two maker manuals above, at rated values. Cold weather raises Voc somewhat, but 90.6 V leaves about 59 V of margin under 150 V. This holds only for the V3.0 hardware the manual describes; the kit listing still says 650 W max.

findings.label: Solar input limit and included cable
findings.value: MPPT 12–70 V, 18 A, 500 W max on the XT60 input; MC4-to-XT60 solar cable in the box
findings.source_title: ALLPOWERS S2000 Portable Power Station review – checks my boxes for a 1500Wh power station (The Gadgeteer, Matt Gregersen)
findings.note: Spec list from Matt Gregersen's review. Battery 1,500 Wh, AC 2,000 W continuous. Arithmetic with SP037 V3.0: one panel (45.3 V, 11.45 A) fits. Two in series = 90.6 V, over 70 V. Two in parallel = 22.9 A, over 18 A. A second SP037 also adds at most 100 W before the 500 W cap. Gregersen saw only about 30 W from solar in cloudy December weather.
